{{short description|Solid-state physicist}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=December 2021}}

'''Gilbert''' "'''Gil'''" '''George Lonzarich''' (born 1945)<ref name="PhysBl1991">{{cite journal
 |doi=10.1002/phbl.19910470317
 |title=Preisverleihungen 1991
 |year=1991
 |journal=Phys. Bl.
 |volume=47
 |pages=230|doi-access=free
 }}</ref> is a [[Solid-state physics|solid-state physicist]] and Emeritus Professor of the [[University of Cambridge]]. He is particularly noted for his work on superconducting and magnetic materials carried out at the [[Cavendish Laboratory]].

== Life ==
Lonzarich received his BA degree from [[University of California, Berkeley]] (1967), his M.S. from the [[University of Minnesota]] (1970) and his Ph.D. degree from [[University of British Columbia]] (1973). Starting as a postdoc, he has held positions at the University of Cambridge. Since 1997 he is a professor at the [[Cavendish Laboratory]], where he heads the quantum matter group.<ref name="cam.ac.uk">{{cite web |url=http://www.qm.phy.cam.ac.uk/lonzarich/ |title=Department of Physics, Cavendish Laboratory |publisher=University of Cambridge, Department of Physics |accessdate=25 January 2017 |archive-date=6 October 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101006191039/http://www.qm.phy.cam.ac.uk/lonzarich/ |url-status=dead }}</ref>

== Research ==
The research of Lonzarich focuses on solids where the interaction between electrons can lead to unconventional states of matter. His work has addressed different material classes, including itinerant magnets (such as MnSi),<ref name="Pfleiderer1997">{{cite journal
 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevB.55.8330
 |title=Magnetic quantum phase transition in MnSi under hydrostatic pressure
 |year=1997
 |last1=Pfleiderer|first1=C.
 |last2=McMullan|first2=G.J.
 |last3=Julian|first3=S.R.
 |last4=Lonzarich|first4=G.G.
 |journal=Phys. Rev. B
 |volume=55
 |issue=13
 |pages=8330–8338 |bibcode=1997PhRvB..55.8330P}}</ref> heavy-fermion materials,<ref name="Mathur1998">{{cite journal
 |doi=10.1038/27838
 |title=Magnetically mediated superconductivity in heavy fermion compounds
 |year=1998
 |last1=Mathur|first1=N.D.
 |last2=Grosche|first2=F.M.
 |last3=Julian|first3=S.R.
 |last4=Walker|first4=I.R.
 |last5=Freye|first5=D.M.
 |last6=Haselwimmer|first6=R.K.W.
 |last7=Lonzarich|first7=G.G.
 |journal=Nature
 |volume=394
 |issue=6688
 |pages=39–43 |bibcode=1998Natur.394...39M|s2cid=52837444
 }}</ref><ref name="Taillefer1988">{{cite journal
 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.60.1570
 |title=Heavy-fermion quasiparticles in UPt3
 |year=1988
 |last1=Taillefer|first1=L.
 |last2=Lonzarich|first2=G.G.
 |journal=Phys. Rev. Lett.
 |volume=60
 |issue=15
 |pages=1570–1573|pmid=10038074
 |bibcode=1988PhRvL..60.1570T}}</ref> and ferroelectrics.<ref name="Rowley2014">{{cite journal
 |doi=10.1038/nphys2924
 |title=Ferroelectric quantum criticality
 |year=2014
 |last1=Rowley|first1=S.E.
 |last2=Spalek|first2=L.J.
 |last3=Smith|first3=R.P.
 |last4=Dean|first4=M.P.M.
 |last5=Itoh|first5=M.
 |last6=Scott|first6=J.F.
 |last7=Lonzarich|first7=G.G.
 |last8=Saxena|first8=S.S.
 |journal=Nature Physics
 |volume=10
 |issue=5
 |pages=367–372|arxiv=0903.1445|bibcode=2014NatPh..10..367R|s2cid=120096268
 }}</ref> One groundbreaking result for the field of [[Unconventional superconductor|unconventional superconductivity]] was the demonstration that the suppression of antiferromagnetic order in [[heavy fermion material|heavy-fermion materials]], i.e. a quantum-critical point, can induce superconductivity.<ref name="Mathur1998" />

Important aspects of the experiments of Lonzarich's group are crystal growth, ultra-low temperatures (mK temperatures), high-pressure experiments, and [[quantum oscillations]] (continuing the work of [[David Shoenberg]]).<ref name="Gibney2017">{{cite journal
 |doi=10.1038/549448a
 |title=A quantum pioneer unlocks matter's hidden secrets
 |year=2017
 |last1=Gibney|first1=E.
 |journal=Nature
 |volume=549
 |issue=7673
 |pages=448–450|bibcode=2017Natur.549..448G|doi-access=free
 }}</ref>

Notable former students in the group of Lonzarich include [[Piers Coleman]], [[Louis Taillefer]],<ref name="Taillefer1988" /> [[Andrew P. Mackenzie|Andrew MacKenzie]], and [[Christian Pfleiderer]].<ref name="Pfleiderer1997" /><ref name="Gibney2017" />

== Awards ==
* [[Fellow of the Royal Society]] (1989)
* [[EPS Europhysics Prize]] (1989)<ref name="cam.ac.uk" />
* [[Max Born Prize]] (1991)<ref name="PhysBl1991" /><ref name="cam.ac.uk" />
* [[Faraday Medal and Prize|Guthrie Medal]] (2007)<ref name="cam.ac.uk" />
* [[Rumford Medal]] (2010)
* [[Kamerlingh Onnes Prize]] (2015)<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.m2s-2015.ch/kamerlingh-onnes-prize.php |title=Kamerlingh Onnes Prize |publisher=M2S Conference 2015 |accessdate=25 January 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181010210840/http://www.m2s-2015.ch/kamerlingh-onnes-prize.php |archive-date=10 October 2018 |url-status=dead }}</ref>
